chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ يُونُسَ، عَنْ حَرِيزٍ، عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنِ الْحَلَالِ وَالْحَرَامِ فَقَالَ: حَلَالُ مُحَمَّدٍ حَلَالٌ أَبَدًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَحَرَامُهُ حَرَامٌ أَبَدًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ، لَا يَكُونُ غَيْرُهُ وَلَا يَأْتِي غَيْرُهُ، وَقَالَ: قَالَ عَلِيُّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: مَا أَحَدٌ ابْتَدَعَ بِدْعَةً إِلَّا تَرَكَ بِهَا سُنَّةً

translations.en: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Halal and the Haram, so he said: The Halal of Muhammad is Halal forever until the Day of Judgment, and his Haram is Haram forever until the Day of Judgment, there will be no other [law] and no other [law] will come, and he said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: No one has innovated a Bid'a (innovation) except that he has abandoned a Sunnah (prophetic tradition) by doing so.

en.summary: This hadith establishes the permanence and exclusivity of the divine law (Sharia) brought by Prophet Muhammad, asserting that his Halal and Haram are eternal and will not be replaced. It further links the concept of Bid'a (innovation) in religion to the abandonment of established Sunnah, as stated by Imam Ali.
en.seo_question: What is the relationship between innovation (Bid'a) and the abandonment of Sunnah in Shia theology?
